newsitem.title: RUSSIA: RUSSIAN H1 1997 PASSENGER, CARGO VOLUMES FALL.
newsitem.headline: RUSSIAN H1 1997 PASSENGER, CARGO VOLUMES FALL.

text.p: Russian airlines carried 10.8 million passengers during first six months of this year compared with 12.5 million in the same period of 1996, the head of the Federal Aviation Service (FAS) said on Tuesday.
Gennady Zaitsev told the FAS board meeting that Russian carriers' cargo shipments also fell to 117,350 tonnes between January and June, 1997, against 132,360 tonnes during the same period last year.

FAS experts said the drop in passenger and cargo volumes was connected with payment problems among many Russian firms, with high fuel and ticket costs, and the lack of financial support for civil aviation overall from the state.
Zaitsev also said seven aircraft crashes had been registered in Russia in the first half of the year.
"Sixty six people were killed in these crashes," he said, adding that in the same year-ago period, four crashes killed 35 people. In the first half of 1995 five plane crashes killed 43 people.
A FAS report said that 79 percent of the crashes during the first half of the year were due to human error, including aircraft, air traffic control and technical personnel.
Plane malfunctions caused 17 percent of the crashes during the same period.
